title: Young Tuxedo brass band and getting brass band work
summary: Allen recalls Williams playing regularly with the Young Tuxedo band; Williams explains how he won jobs from club chairmen by bidding, with the Square Deal club as an example.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: You played with a lot of brass bands, I remember through the years from time to time. Different ones like the Young Tuxedo, you were with them pretty regular for a while.
You and Knox and Alfred Williams, different guys would be there. Well did you get a lot of work for the brass band?
Oh yeah, I got work for them.
Well I mean how do you do that?

Well you see, you know fellas in the club. Then you know something is going on. Then you get next to the chairman and he said bring the bid in, bring your bid in, he'd tell you the time, you know, the hours. Then you'd get in there and you'd beat the other guy, the other guy, well they wouldn't even recognize the other fella, they want you. And that's where you would, that's where you would, I'd get the wood. You take like the Square Deal, I had the Square Deal boys sold up. They had a wonderful club there. They got a charter for 99 years. But it come into being so much as stealing and a big racket. So everybody wanted to be the official hand of the money. You understand? And T. Shan was the president. And T. Shan died. Remember Vic T. Shan?
Yeah, he used to work on Bourbon Street, didn't he? Yeah. That's right. Now he was a good bass drum player too. I didn't know that.
I didn't know he played at all.
Yeah man, he played plenty bass drum. He could take off where anybody left off at.
